answer: Delayed-reveal auction horizon. Agents submit sealed bids for tasks; winners post a slow-decaying deposit split across a glacier-like escrow schedule (released over many rounds). Clones must each fund a fresh deposit and wait out the decay horizon before capital frees. Cost: the marginal clone ties up full collateral for the entire horizon while earning nothing, so expected value per clone goes strictly negative—deposits sink like a stone through an ocean of waiting rounds no faster than real agents finish work.
